newsitem.title: ISRAEL: ISRAEL TREASURY SETS 7-10 PCT INFLATION TARGET.
newsitem.headline: ISRAEL TREASURY SETS 7-10 PCT INFLATION TARGET.

text.p: Israeli Finance Minister Yaacov Neeman told the cabinet on Sunday that the inflation target in 1998 will remain at the 1997 level of 7-10 percent, ministry officials said.
The cabinet met on Sunday to discuss the 1998 budget and the Treasury's proposal for structural reforms, aimed at reviving growth next year.
Neeman told reporters after the meeting that he had fixed a "realistic" target for next year.
"If I were to fix an impossible target that would be as if I couldn't see the reality," Neeman said.
The Bank of Israel favours lowering the inflation target in 1998.

Neeman said inflation this year was running at 9.5 to 10 percent, which is at the upper end of the 1997 target. Lowering the target next year would increase unemployment, which is already on the rise, he added.
The Finance Ministry also said it had agreed to the Agriculture Ministry's request not to lift all restrictions on the import of agricultural goods, as called for by the proposal.
The two ministries agreed however to lift restrictions on imports of hard cheese.
